Lesson 8: Market Area Analysis for Retail and Service Locations: Huff and MCI Models

Published

November 3, 2025

Modified

October 20, 2026

According to Huff, trade area is defined as “a geographically delineated region containing potential customers for whom there exists a probability greater than zero of their purchasing a given class of products or services offered for sale by a particular firm or by a particular agglomeration of firms”. Several methods to delineate a store trade area have been proposed over the years. For drive-time or travel distance analysis method, the trade area is delineated according to how far or how long the customers are willing to travel to patronise the store. Another commonly used method is the Huff Model which assumes that consumer decisions are probabilistic and not deterministic.

In this lesson, you will learn the basic concepts Spatial Interaction and Huff and MCI Models for trade area delineation and analysis.

Content

  • Basic Concepts of Spatial Interaction
  • Introducing Huff model
    • Basic concepts and method
    • Calibrating Huff model
    • Interpreting Huff model results
  • Introducing Multiplicative Competitive Interaction Model (MCI)
    • Basic concepts and method
    • Calibrating MCI model
    • Interpreting MCI model results
